newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Mozambique approves "world's largest" private park.
newsitem.headline: Mozambique approves "world's largest" private park.

text.p: Mozambique has granted final approval for a private game reserve which the U.S.-based company behind the project claims is the largest in the world.
"The conservation project encompasses 234,000 hectares (580,000 acres) in the Maputuland region of southern Mozambique, Blanchard Mozambique Enterprises (BME) said in a statement on Friday.

U.S. millionaire James Blanchard III, who gave financial backing to the former rebel movement Renamo during the 17-year civil war against President Joaquim Chissano's government, presented an outline of the project to Chissano in October 1995.
"After extensive review, the government approved the project as a means to stimulate economic growth while protecting a globally important eco-system," the statement said.
BME said this was the largest public game reserve and conservation project ever transferred to private management and funding.
"The project is also unique for its 90 km (56 miles) of pristine, Indian Ocean beach front, making it the only, sun, sea and safari experience in Africa."
The reserve will cover a large chunk of the Mozambican district of Matutuine, which adjoins South Africa's coast.
The region's large concentration of wildlife was depleted during the civil war between the government and the South African-backed Renamo in the 1980s.
Blanchard plans to restock the reserve, but it will be expensive. One black rhino costs about $55,000.
"Through proper wildlife management, this area will draw the necessary tourism dollars to provide for maximum employment of the local population while preserving the eco-system," BME said.
In 1995 Blanchard said he would try to raise $800 million in investment for the project from a variety of sources but the latest statement gives no indication of the projected costs.
Apart from a luxury hotel, game lodges, a golf course and an off-shore floating casino, the plan includes a 165-km (100-mile) railway costing more than $52 million.
